record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Can one construct explicit families of local quasi-holomorphic curves from the complex disk into a quasi Riemann surface, for example when the ambient 2n-dimensional space is the sphere S^{2n}, so that local conformal-field-theoretic structure can be studied there?

evidence.quote: Explicit constructions of local quasi holomorphic curves are needed, say for M = S^2n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $M$ be a smooth oriented Riemannian $2n$-dimensional manifold. Following the framework of quasi Riemann surfaces, one associates to $M$ a quasi Riemann surface $Q(M)$: a (typically infinite-dimensional) space built from integral $(n-1)$-currents on $M$, equipped with a skew-hermitian form and a complex structure $J$ that mimic, in higher dimension, the period pairing and the Hodge star on a Riemann surface. A quasi holomorphic curve in $Q(M)$ is a map $f : \Sigma \to Q(M)$ from an ordinary Riemann surface $\Sigma$ (or an open subset of the complex disk $D \subset \mathbb{C}$, in the local case) into $Q(M)$ that intertwines the complex structures and preserves the skew-hermitian forms on integral currents. Such curves serve as local probes that pull back functions, differential forms, and conformal tensors on $Q(M)$ to ordinary objects on the Riemann surface $\Sigma$, thereby giving local two-dimensional conformal-field-theoretic data on $Q(M)$.

Problem. Construct explicit families of local quasi holomorphic curves $f : D \to Q(M)$ from the complex disk $D$ into the quasi Riemann surface $Q(M)$ in the case
$$M = S^{2n},$$
the round $2n$-sphere. In particular, exhibit a family rich enough that pullback along the family represents functions, forms, and conformal tensors on $Q(S^{2n})$ as coherent collections of ordinary holomorphic data on Riemann surfaces, so that the local conformal-field-theoretic structure of $Q(S^{2n})$ can be analyzed concretely.
artifact.status_search_result: The notion of quasi Riemann surfaces and quasi holomorphic curves was introduced by Friedan, who explicitly states that constructing local quasi holomorphic curves, in particular for $M = S^{2n}$, is needed and remains to be carried out. No subsequent work establishing such explicit constructions was found.

status_evidence.title: Quasi Riemann surfaces II. Questions, comments, speculations
status_evidence.snippet: Local quasi holomorphic curves are local probes of the quasi Riemann surface; explicit constructions are needed, e.g. for M = S^{2n}.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit local quasi-holomorphic curve constructions for S^{2n} are listed as an open problem.
